text:
maria: quick proposal — split model intake into two explicit paths: "fast-smoke" (cheap, sub-second checks to catch runtime/format/IO issues) and "full-bench" (async, heavy perf + quality sweep). low friction deploys rely on smoke; production promotion requires full-bench. thoughts?

sam: +1 on split. question on ownership: do we build a single intake service that routes by policy, or two focused services with a small shared contract?

maria: leaning two services + a tiny shared contract (artifact pointer, manifest metadata, expected inference interface). routing done at gateway based on model tags/size and an optional header (X-intake-mode).

jules: two services feels better operationally: fast-smoke co-located with ingress (low-latency), full-bench runs on batch fleet. con: duplication of parsing/manifest validation logic across both stacks.

kevin: duplication will be a problem over time. propose factoring parsing + manifest validation into a small language-agnostic lib (python + go bindings) and expose a thin RPC for legacy stacks. smoke path should be able to call lib in-process; bench fleet can call RPC or use the lib image.

anita: big tradeoff is sequencing: do we block serving until smoke passes? do we block traffic routing until full-bench finishes? how do we handle canaries?

maria: operational plan draft:
- fast-smoke: block serving for public endpoints (no incoming traffic until PASS). checks: artifact integrity, model input/output shape, a 3-sample inference against runtime, simple KV/warmup hookup. returns PASS/FAIL + warnings. sets registry status = "smoke-passed" (or "smoke-failed").
- full-bench: async. runs suite: latency P50/P95, throughput curves, GPU memory & allocation profile, quantization regression checks, and eval-set accuracy/regression metrics. posts detailed report and a generated "verification token" if thresholds met. on success registry status -> "verified".

jules: this matches what I expected. we should be explicit about routing: "smoke-passed" models can be routed to dev/staging and ephemeral test clusters; only "verified" models promoted to production routing policies and SLA-backed nodes.

bench-bot: Heads-up — our current golden baselines require: P95 <= baseline * 1.25, accuracy drop <= 2% absolute on representative eval. Bench job will fail if metrics missing.

kevin: implementation notes:
- manifest v1: declarative JSON with fields {runtime, entry_point, input_schema, warmup_calls, quantized: bool, tags}. validate via JSON Schema.
- provide a lightweight docker image that mounts the model artifact + validator lib for bench fleet; plus an RPC for legacy stacks. avoid syncing heavy artifacts over RPC.

jules: agree on manifest versioning. we should embed an immutable model fingerprint (sha256 of artifact + manifest) for idempotency and retries.

maria: example manifest snippet (proposal):
```
{
  "manifest_version": "v1",
  "model_name": "my-llm",
  "runtime": "torch",
  "entry_point": "/serve/run.py",
  "input_schema": { "type": "string" },
  "warmup_calls": 5,
  "tags": ["small", "embedding"]
}
```

anita: failure visibility is important. propose structured error codes surfaced in the registry UI + Console alerts, e.g. SMOKE_INVALID_MANIFEST, SMOKE_RUNTIME_CRASH, BENCH_METRIC_MISSING, BENCH_REGRESSION. bench results should include diffs vs golden and links to raw logs.

sam: monitoring + SLOs: alert if smoke fail rate > 3% for new uploads (maybe indicates a broken SDK), and alert if bench backlog > 12h. cost control: cap bench runs per org per day; require manual approval for very large models.

kevin: on RPC latencies — bench path should never block on RPC artifact transfer. bench fleet should pull artifacts from object storage using the provided pointer; RPC only for manifest validation/short metadata queries. keep heavy IO out of control plane.

jules: rollout plan idea:
1) feature-flag the split in intake gateway, default fallback to single-path for 2 weeks.
2) run smoke locally in ingress path; fan-out bench jobs to bench fleet (no promotion gating yet).
3) after 2 weeks, enable registry gating: require "smoke-passed" for serving; after additional 2 weeks enable "verified" gating for production routing.

maria: corner cases:
- small models that run fast: can opt-out of full-bench via "bench-opt-out" tag if org accepts risk + signs waiver.
- experimental uploads: allow "ad-hoc" uploads that don't hit registry (dev-only).
- schema evolution: manifest v2 will contain hardware hints; ensure validator library supports backward compatibility.

anita: retry/backoff & idempotency: bench jobs should be idempotent keyed by fingerprint; use exponential backoff for transient infra errors; cap retries to 3. surface final failure reason.

kevin: dev ergonomics: expose a local `rw-intake validate` CLI that runs the smoke checks and linting so authors can iterate before upload.

maria: next steps: I'll write an RFC covering contract (manifest schema), validation library API, bench job contract, registry states, and rollout plan. prototype of smoke lib + CLI in 2 weeks. owners: maria (intake gateway), kevin (validator lib), jules (bench fleet integration), anita (registry/UX), sam (SLOs/alerts).

sam: sounds good. please add acceptance criteria in RFC: e.g., smoke latency <= 200ms added to ingress path, bench backlog <= 6h target, clear regression alerting.

maria: will do. ping me if you want a slot in next week's arch sync. :wave:
